samples.brief: Framework verify (n=2): a 150-250 word piece on 'an AI tool that turns Hindi voice notes into meeting minutes' that follows the card's steps in order, each step labelled in square brackets. Illustrative figures are allowed when labelled, as the card's own mini_example does, so every step carries real copy.
samples.text:
Webinar: "Meeting minutes ab bolkar likhiye" (Hindi voice notes to minutes). Everything below is illustrative.

[Origin story] (about 15 min) March 2025: a Pune logistics founder lost Rs 1.8 lakh because "Thursday ko final karenge" lived only in an untyped Hindi voice note. Next meeting he spoke a recap into WhatsApp: a tool returned minutes in 90 seconds. Eleven meetings on: no disputes.

[The Vehicle] (about 15 min) The method: Bol, Tag, Bhej. Bol a two-minute recap after the meeting. Tag each decision with owner and date, aloud. Bhej the minutes on WhatsApp within the hour. Big Domino: "Minutes are a speaking job, not a typing job."

[Internal beliefs] (about 15 min) "Mujhse tech nahi hota." Proof: a front-desk executive new to AI records a recap live; minutes in three taps.

[External beliefs] (about 15 min) "AI Hinglish samajhta hi nahi." Proof: a mixed Hindi-English note with names and dates, run live, showing what it got right and two missed words.

[The Stack] (about 30 min) Tool, 3 months: Rs 2,700. Add template pack Rs 999: total Rs 3,699. Add onboarding call Rs 1,500: total Rs 5,199. Add WhatsApp support, 30 days, Rs 1,200: total Rs 6,399. Today Rs 2,499, with a 30-day refund if your first five minutes are unusable. Ends Friday 23 October, 11:59 pm IST.

[Close and questions] One action: "Scan the code, start before Friday night." Objections arrive as questions ("Data kahan store hota hai?"): answer with [storage location, from the privacy page] on screen.
samples.writer_note: Retest after the 'weak, writer fault' verdict. Fixes: the Vehicle is now a named method (Bol, Tag, Bhej) that carries the Big Domino, not the product pipeline; the external block holds ONE belief (Hinglish) and the data question moves to the close as a worked objection; the Stack and the close are written as lines, not instructions (running total after each item, price, refund, dated deadline); the origin is a labelled illustrative case with a year, a loss and a result. Every figure and the founder are invented for the demo and marked 'illustrative'; 'each item sells alone at this price' must be true before real use. The three 'secrets' are not named (the card says its source does not). Step times are the card's. 249 words, inside 150-250.

samples.brief: Meta ad copy (Instagram and Facebook feed) for a Pune D2C millet-snack brand's trial pack (Rs 299, free shipping) aimed at working parents aged 28-40 in metro cities who do not know the brand; English with a light Hinglish touch; 3 variants with different angles (the kids' tiffin problem, ingredient proof, the trial price), each with primary text whose first 125 characters carry the hook and offer, a headline of 27 characters or fewer and a CTA button choice; goal: clicks to the trial-pack page.
samples.text:
META AD COPY: millet snack trial pack (Instagram and Facebook feed)

VARIANT 1: the 7 am tiffin question
Angle note (working, not published): pain. Cold audience, problem-aware. Tests whether the daily tiffin decision pulls more clicks than proof or price.
Primary text, visible opening: 7 baje tiffin ka sawaal: aaj kya rakhein? Try our millet snack trial pack, Rs 299, free shipping.
Primary text, body: Sandwich again? Slip a pack of millet snacks into the tiffin and see which dabba comes back empty. Same Rs 299 trial pack, free shipping, on the page.
Headline: Tiffin ke snack ka jawab
Description: A millet snack trial pack from Pune.
CTA button: Shop Now

VARIANT 2: read the label
Angle note (working, not published): proof. Same parents, product-aware only through this ad, label readers. Tests whether the ingredient list earns more trust than the pain hook.
Primary text, visible opening: Label padhte ho? Ours reads: [ingredients as printed on the pack]. Trial pack Rs 299, free shipping.
Primary text, body: The full list is on the pack and on the page: [full ingredient list]. Try one pack for Rs 299, free shipping, then decide.
Headline: Read the label first
Description: Full ingredient list on the page.
CTA button: Learn More

VARIANT 3: the trial price
Angle note (working, not published): offer. Most-aware viewers who just want a low-risk first order. Tests price and free shipping against the other two angles.
Primary text, visible opening: Rs 299, free shipping: a trial pack of millet snacks from Pune, so you can try before you stock up.
Primary text, body: Inside: [N] snacks in [flavours]. Rs 299 with free shipping. Tap Shop Now and the same price is waiting on the page.
Headline: Rs 299 trial, free shipping
Description: Trial pack. Pune. Free shipping.
CTA button: Shop Now
samples.writer_note: Placeholders: [ingredients as printed on the pack], [full ingredient list], [N] snacks and [flavours]: the brief gives no ingredient or pack-contents fact, so none is invented, and no health, nutrition or taste claim is made. The earlier gender slip is gone ('roz ka sirdard' hook replaced by a tiffin-question hook). Three different angles (pain, proof, offer), three different descriptions, CTA buttons Shop Now / Learn More / Shop Now (all lead to the trial-pack page). Openings are 97, 100 and 99 characters; headlines 24, 20 and 27. Each opening was checked from its own file against the Instagram feed 125 limit and each headline against the Facebook feed 27 limit; the whole sheet against the genre lint. Landing page must show the same Rs 299 and free shipping.

samples.brief: Original Hindi indie-pop love song (Devanagari with Roman transliteration) for a Delhi singer-songwriter, about long-distance love over late-night video calls between Delhi and Bengaluru; mukhda of 4 lines with the title phrase in its first line, two antaras of 6 lines each with matching syllable patterns, mukhda repeats after each antara; syllable count marked at the end of every line; no lines borrowed from existing songs.
samples.text:
बफ़रिंग में भी तुम
Buffering Mein Bhi Tum
Hindi indie-pop. Delhi to Bengaluru, late-night video calls.

Syllables are counted as sung, one per vowel beat, at the end of every line.
Counts used: shehar 2, ghar 1, buffering 3, battery 3, calendar 3, doorbell 2.
Rhymes: refrain "lagte ho" (achhe/poore); ghar/par.
Antara 1: baarish/aazmaish, screen/yaqeen, jaata/bhaata.
Antara 2: calendar/safar, saamaan/armaan, baad/fariyaad.
Both antaras run 13, 13, 13, 13, 8, 13.

MUKHDA
बफ़रिंग में भी तुम कितने अच्छे लगते हो (13)
buffering mein bhi tum kitne achhe lagte ho
आधी हँसी पे अटके तुम पूरे लगते हो (13)
aadhi hansi pe atke tum poore lagte ho
दो शहर हैं बीच में, पर इस कॉल पे एक ही घर (13)
do shehar hain beech mein, par is call pe ek hi ghar
बैटरी बस दो परसेंट है, तुम रहना लाइन पर (13)
battery bas do percent hai, tum rehna line par

ANTARA 1
मेरे यहाँ कोहरा, तुम्हारे यहाँ बारिश (13)
mere yahaan kohra, tumhare yahaan baarish
लोग कहते हैं ये दूरी है बस एक आज़माइश (13)
log kehte hain ye doori hai bas ek aazmaish
रज़ाई के अंदर बस इतनी-सी छोटी स्क्रीन (13)
razaai ke andar bas itni-si chhoti screen
उसमें मिलता है तुम्हारे होने का यक़ीन (13)
usmein milta hai tumhare hone ka yaqeen
जब भी नेटवर्क रुक जाता है (8)
jab bhi network ruk jaata hai
तब भी तुम्हारा ही चेहरा मुझे भाता है (13)
tab bhi tumhara hi chehra mujhe bhaata hai

MUKHDA (repeat)

ANTARA 2
एक तारीख़ पे लाल गोला, ये रहा कैलेंडर (13)
ek taareekh pe laal gola, ye raha calendar
आख़िरी है ये हफ़्ता, फिर छोटा-सा सफ़र (13)
aakhiri hai ye hafta, phir chhota-sa safar
तीन घंटे की फ़्लाइट और सिर्फ़ एक ही छोटा सामान (13)
teen ghante ki flight aur sirf ek hi chhota saamaan
बैग तो हल्का है, भारी है बस वो एक अरमान (13)
bag to halka hai, bhaari hai bas wo ek armaan
इस बार सिर्फ़ एक डोरबेल के बाद (8)
is baar sirf ek doorbell ke baad
अब न हैलो-हैलो, न नेटवर्क की फ़रियाद (13)
ab na hello-hello, na network ki fariyaad

MUKHDA (repeat)

FINAL MUKHDA (each line changes a little to land the ending)
अब बफ़रिंग नहीं, तुम अच्छे ही लगते हो (13)
ab buffering nahin, tum achhe hi lagte ho
अब पूरी हँसी के साथ तुम पूरे लगते हो (13)
ab poori hansi ke saath tum poore lagte ho
दो शहर थे बीच में, इस कमरे में एक ही घर (13)
do shehar the beech mein, is kamre mein ek hi ghar
बैटरी दो परसेंट थी, अब तुम हो यहीं पर (13)
battery do percent thi, ab tum ho yahin par
samples.writer_note: Original lines, written from scratch; not searched against existing songs, so a human should search the key phrases ('buffering mein bhi tum', 'do percent hai, tum rehna line par') before release. No placeholders; singer's gender is not given, so verbs avoid gendered forms. Syllables hand-counted line by line from a hyphenated transliteration (a scratch script only counted the chunks); all 20 unique lines match their marked counts and antara 1 and 2 match 13, 13, 13, 13, 8, 13. Earlier fault (no rhyme in the antaras, broken word order) fixed: each antara is three exact couplets (baarish/aazmaish, screen/yaqeen, jaata/bhaata; calendar/safar, saamaan/armaan, baad/fariyaad), the mukhda carries a refrain and ghar/par, and the last antara line sets up the next mukhda. Per the card's pitfall on AI-assisted lyrics, tell the client these lyrics were AI-assisted. 442 words including both scripts, under the 450 lint cap.

samples.brief: Instagram caption plus 5 talking points for a Bengaluru fitness creator's paid collaboration with a Mysuru millet-protein brand; audience: her followers, office-goers aged 22-35; Hinglish (Roman script) in her casual voice; 80-150 words; 'Ad' label in the first line in addition to the Paid partnership tag; one honest limitation; discount code with a 7-day deadline; claims limited to the brand's approved list (12 g protein per serving).
samples.text:
CAPTION (Instagram; switch the Paid partnership tag on in the app as well)

Ad | Paid partnership with [@brand]

4 baje wali bhookh: office ki sabse sachchi emergency. Samosa wali trolley aati hai aur sabka focus chala jaata hai, hai na?

Pichhle [N] din se drawer mein [product name] hai, biscuit ki jagah. [One real detail: when you reach for it, and the taste or crunch in your words.] Number simple hai: ek serving mein 12 g protein.

Mera rule: yeh snack hai, khaane ki jagah nahi. Aur 12 g ek serving ka hai, poore din ka nahi.

Code [CODE] se [discount] milega, Thursday 22 October raat 11:59 baje tak. Link bio mein.

#MilletSnack #OfficeSnack #BengaluruFitness

TALKING POINTS (video version, say in her own words)

- First sentence, before anything else: "Ad, paid partnership with [brand]." Keep the label on screen for the whole brand segment.
- The 4 pm moment: show the drawer and the pack on the desk. Say what she reached for before and what she reaches for now, only as far as it is true for her.
- Taste or crunch: one honest line, on camera, after she has actually eaten it.
- The one product claim: "Ek serving mein 12 g protein." Nothing about weight loss, muscle gain or health results. If she adds any nutrition advice, her qualification goes up front.
- Say the limit out loud (snack, not a meal; 12 g is per serving), then the code [CODE] for [discount], valid till Thursday 22 October, 11:59 pm.
samples.writer_note: Placeholders: [@brand], [product name], [N] days, [CODE], [discount] and one 'real detail' slot (when she reaches for it and the taste or crunch in her words): the brief gives no use history or taste fact, and a made-up one would be a false endorsement. The only product claim is the approved 12 g protein per serving; the honest limit (snack, not a meal; 12 g is per serving) is stated in her voice, not as a label hedge. Code deadline: Thursday 22 October 2026, 11:59 pm, 7 days after a Thursday 15 October post. Disclosure 'Ad | Paid partnership with [@brand]' is line 1; the platform tag must also be on. No nutrition advice beyond the label figure; if she adds any, her qualification goes up front. Caption alone is 102 words (brief 80-150); caption plus talking points 249.

samples.brief: 30-second YouTube skippable in-stream ad plus a 6-second bumper for a Kochi Ayurvedic hair-oil brand launching online in North India; audience: women 25-40 in Delhi NCR; Hindi VO with English supers; two-column AV script with timings; brand and product shown before 5 seconds; no medical or growth claims; text assets within YouTube limits; goal: click 'Shop now' to the brand site.
samples.text:
VIDEO AD SCRIPT: [Brand] Ayurvedic Hair Oil, Kochi

SPEC HEADER
Versions: 30 s skippable in-stream and 6 s bumper (YouTube, 16:9).
Audience: women 25-40, Delhi NCR. Objective: Shop now clicks to the brand site.
One message: Kochi-made [Brand] Ayurvedic Hair Oil is now online in Delhi NCR.
Sound off: supers carry every spoken idea. VO: Hindi, warm woman's voice, "aap" register.
Mandatory super, last 3 s: [statutory line from client compliance].
No hair growth, hair fall or treatment claims. Real actors and product only; no AI imagery.

30-SECOND VERSION
| Time | Visual | VO / sync (Hindi) | Super (English) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00-0:05 | Sunday morning, a Gurugram flat. Phone lights up: "Maa", speaker on. Beside it a [Brand] bottle, seal intact, in frame from 0:01. A woman in her 30s glances at it. | माँ (फ़ोन पर): "बेटा, तेल लगाया?" वह: "हाँ मम्मी, लगा लिया।" | "Maa: Tel lagaya?" At 0:02: [Brand] Ayurvedic Hair Oil. Made in Kochi. |
| 0:05-0:13 | She breaks the seal, warms oil between her palms, massages her scalp, eyes closed. | इस संडे सच में लगा लीजिए। हथेली में थोड़ा-सा तेल, और दस मिनट सिर्फ़ अपने नाम। | Sunday. 10 minutes. Just yours. |
| 0:13-0:21 | Close shots: label, cap turning, oil into her palm. Line from Kochi to Delhi NCR. | कोच्चि में बना आयुर्वेदिक हेयर ऑयल। [मुख्य सामग्री, लेबल के अनुसार]। | Made in Kochi. [Ingredient line as on the label] |
| 0:21-0:26 | The phone buzzes: "Maa". She answers, tilts the phone: towel on her head, bottle beside her. | माँ: "अच्छा?" वह: "हाँ मम्मी, इस बार सच में।" | This time, really. |
| 0:26-0:30 | End card: logo, bottle, Shop now button, site. Silence from 0:29. | अब दिल्ली एनसीआर में ऑनलाइन। Shop now पर टैप कीजिए। | Now online in Delhi NCR. Shop now. [Brand site] [Statutory line] |

6-SECOND BUMPER (its own idea)
| Time | Visual | VO (Hindi) | Super (English) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00-0:03 | Wall calendar, a Sunday circled in red pen. A hand sets the [Brand] bottle on the circle, in frame from 0:01. | संडे यानी [Brand] का आयुर्वेदिक तेल। | Sunday = [Brand] Ayurvedic Hair Oil |
| 0:03-0:06 | Pack shot: bottle, logo, button. | कोच्चि से, अब दिल्ली एनसीआर में। | Made in Kochi. Now in Delhi NCR. Shop now. [Statutory line] |

TEXT ASSETS (video action campaign)
Headline: Sunday champi, Kochi se
Long headline: Kochi mein bana Ayurvedic hair oil, ab Delhi NCR mein. Sunday ki champi ke liye.
Description: Ayurvedic hair oil, made in Kochi. Online order karein, [confirm delivery area].
Call to action: Shop now
samples.writer_note: New creative after the 'generic courier open, logistics-only reason, contradictory middle beat, bumper replays the open' verdict: the 30 s opens on the mother's Sunday phone call asking 'tel lagaya?' with the sealed bottle in frame from 0:01 and the brand lockup at 0:02, pays off in the last call ('this time, really'), and the middle beat (she oils her own hair, 'ten minutes just yours') matches its VO. The 6 s bumper is a different idea (a bottle set down on a circled Sunday). Placeholders: [Brand], [Brand site], [statutory line from client compliance], [Ingredient line as on the label] / [मुख्य सामग्री, लेबल के अनुसार], delivery area to be confirmed: the brief supplies none. No claim beyond 'Ayurvedic' and 'made in Kochi'. The Gurugram flat and the 'Maa' calls are staging choices for the client to approve. Text assets: headline 23/30, long headline 80/90, description 80/90, CTA 8/10, each checked from its own file. Sheet is 396 words against the 400 lint cap.

samples.brief: Shoot outline for a Hinglish travel vlogger's 12-15 minute YouTube vlog 'Rs 1,500 mein Varanasi ka ek din' (one day in Varanasi on Rs 1,500); audience: student travellers; Hinglish (Roman); 300-500 words with the promise, two cold-open options, 6-8 planned moments with a running budget tracker, questions for a boatman and a chai seller, a rain plan B, ending and shot checklist; goal: a story the editor can cut.
samples.text:
VLOG OUTLINE: "Rs 1,500 mein Varanasi ka ek din" (12-15 min, Hinglish)

PROMISE
Ek student ka poora Varanasi din Rs 1,500 mein. Sawaal: raat tak budget bachega? Title: "Rs 1,500 mein Varanasi ka ek din". Thumbnail: face, teen Rs 500 ke note, ghat peeche.

COLD OPEN (pick one, on location)
1. Assi Ghat ki seedhi, subah 5:20, teen note haath mein: "Ek din. Rs 1,500. Dekhte hain Banaras raat tak kitna chhodta hai."
2. Boatman ke saamne, bargain ke beech: "Bhaiya, 300 mein ho jayega?" Hard cut to title.

PLANNED MOMENTS (tracker on screen after each; caps are plans)
1. Assi Ghat sunrise, kulhad chai (cap Rs 30, left 1,470). Why: sets the rule. Say: "chai pehle, plan baad mein". B-roll: steam, kulhad, ghat par yoga.
2. Shared boat to Dashashwamedh (cap Rs 300, left 1,170). Why: first real test of the budget. Say: daam pehle poochho, baaki yatri se share. B-roll: oar, ghat panorama.
3. Kachori-sabzi, jalebi in the galis (cap Rs 80, left 1,090). Why: a student can eat well cheap. Say: ek plate, kitni garam. B-roll: kadhai, jalebi.
4. BHU campus walk, e-rickshaw (cap Rs 150, left 940). Why: the student angle, free places. Say: kya free, kya paid. B-roll: gate, lawn, ride POV.
5. Thali lunch, then lassi and paan (cap Rs 270, left 670). Why: the budget turns tight. Say (re-hook): "Rs 670 mein teen cheezein baaki: aarti ki jagah, raat ka khana, wapsi ka kiraya." B-roll: thali overhead, tracker close-up.
6. Evening aarti, Dashashwamedh: steps Rs 0 or boat seat cap Rs 200 (left 670 or 470). Why: the payoff scene; the choice shows the trade-off. Say: steps ya nao, kyun. B-roll: diye, ghanta, dhuan.
7. Dinner, tamatar chaat and baati-chokha (cap Rs 250, left 420 or 220 for the ride back). Why: the number everyone waits for. Say: final tracker. B-roll: tawa, plate, bill.

QUESTIONS ON CAMERA (aap throughout)
Boatman:
- Aap kitne saal se nao chala rahe hain? Pehli sawari kaisi thi?
- Subah aur shaam ki Ganga mein kya farak lagta hai?
- Ek student Rs 1,500 mein din bitaaye, to aap use kahan bhejenge?
Chai seller:
- Aapke yahan sabse purana grahak kaun hai?
- Subah ki pehli kulhad kab banti hai?
- Banarasi chai mein aisa kya hai jo doosre shehar mein nahi milta?

PLAN B (barish ya paani chadha)
Nao band to galiyon ka walk, covered chai stall, aarti chhat ya shed ke neeche se, jahan mile. Paani chadha ho to nao mat lo: safety pehle.

SPONSOR
None. Agar aaye: label on screen shuru se.

ENDING
Payoff: final tracker, "Rs [X] bacha".
Closing line 1: "Rs 1,500 mein poora Banaras nahi, par uska dil mil gaya."
Closing line 2: "Kal subah phir nikal jaaun, aisa mann hai."
CTA: comment mein batao agla shehar kaunsa.

SHOT CHECKLIST
[ ] Sunrise wide  [ ] Kulhad close  [ ] Oar aur paani  [ ] Notes ginna  [ ] Bill har stop par
[ ] Dukaandaar ke haath (poochh kar)  [ ] Diye paani par  [ ] Seedhiyon par kadam
[ ] Selfie reaction  [ ] Thumbnail frame
samples.writer_note: Budget figures are planned caps, not claimed prices, and the arithmetic reconciles (1,500 less 30, 300, 80, 150, 270 leaves 670; aarti 0 or 200 then dinner 250 leaves 420 or 220 for the ride back). The earlier false re-hook is replaced by one that matches the numbers (three things left for Rs 670). Every beat now has a 'why it matters', say-points and B-roll; feminine nouns take 'ki' (evening aarti, not 'ka'); questions use 'aap' throughout. The only live-price risk is the boat: the outline says to ask first and share. Plan B has a flood-safety line. No sponsor in the brief, so the sponsor block says None with a label note. Final tracker is Rs [X] because it is only known after the shoot. 490 words, brief asks 300-500.

samples.brief: Topic: TOPICS[2] = an AI tool that turns Hindi voice notes into meeting minutes. Surface: promotional email subject line to people who tried the tool free (plat:email_subject_line, fields subject line chars+words, punctuation marks, emojis: 60 chars, 9 words, 3 punctuation). No price, discount, plan, user count or date was supplied, so every number is a [placeholder] the brand fills with the real checkout price. Each of the five hooks is a different offer mechanic (monthly price, percent off, introductory term, free extra, Hinglish price) and each one names the thing sold as the meeting-minutes tool, so 'minutes' can never be read as minutes of audio. Billing terms and the offer end date go in the preheader.
samples.text:
1. Hindi meeting minutes at Rs [price]/month: [N] meetings
   Template: [Product] at Rs [price]: [what's included].
2. Flat [N]% off our Hindi minutes tool till [date]
   Template: Flat [N]% off [category] till [date, time].
3. Hindi minutes tool: Rs [price]/month for [N] months, [terms]
   Template: [Product] for Rs [EMI]/month for [N] months, [interest condition]. ([terms] = the billing condition that replaces 'interest' for a subscription)
4. Free [extra] with Hindi minutes plans above Rs [price]
   Template: Free [item] with every [purchase] above Rs [threshold], till [date]. (date moved to the preheader)
5. Sirf Rs [price] mein voice note se meeting minutes
   Template: Sirf Rs [price] mein [product], [what's included] ke saath. (what is included = 'voice note se meeting minutes')
samples.writer_note: Faults named by the earlier judge, addressed: every hook names the product (the old #4 did not); 'minutes' is always 'meeting minutes' or 'minutes tool' (the old #3 read as audio minutes); the five hooks use five different mechanics instead of three low-price lines; the EMI shape keeps its condition slot as [terms]. Hook 4 moves the deadline to the preheader and hook 5 drops 'ke saath' to stay within 9 words. All numbers, extras and terms are placeholders.

samples.brief: Topic: TOPICS[1] = a Pune cloud-kitchen brand launching a high-protein thali. Surface: launch email subject line to the kitchen's subscriber list (plat:email_subject_line, fields subject line chars+words, punctuation marks, emojis: 60 chars, 9 words, 3 punctuation), chosen over Pinterest because the reader is a customer who will order, not a pinner expecting a recipe. The easy part is the ordering and the no-cooking, never the nutrition: no protein grams, weight or health result, no delivery time, step count, price or menu item beyond [N] placeholders the kitchen confirms. Never 'quick' and 'easy' stacked in one line. Each hook removes a different hassle: effort, time, cooking, meal-prep, carrying a tiffin.
samples.text:
1. The lazy way to a high-protein lunch ([N] taps)
   Template: The [lazy / quick] way to [result] ([time]).
2. High-protein thali ordered in [N] minutes, only your phone
   Template: [Result] in [N] minutes, using only [tool you already have]. ('using' dropped to fit 9 words; [N] minutes counts ordering, not delivery)
3. Quick way to get a high-protein lunch, no cooking
   Template: Here's a quick way to [task] without [usual hassle]. (shortened to fit 9 words)
4. High-protein lunch sirf [N] minute mein, bina meal-prep ke
   Template: [Task] sirf [N] minute mein, bina [hassle] ke.
5. High-protein lunch the easy way: [N] steps, no tiffin
   Template: [Result] the easy way: [N] steps, [time] total. ([time] total swapped for 'no tiffin', a second hassle removed)
samples.writer_note: Earlier sample: one idea five ways on Pinterest, where 'lazy way to a high-protein lunch' resolving to a delivery order read as bait. Now the surface is the kitchen's own subscriber email and each hook removes a different hassle (effort, time, cooking, meal-prep, tiffin). The old '3 steps (pick, order, eat)' line is gone; [N] steps is filled by the kitchen from its real ordering flow. 'Eat high-protein' avoided. No nutrition number anywhere.

samples.brief: Topic: TOPICS[0] = a Jaipur CA firm that handles GST notices for D2C brands. samples.brief: Topic: TOPICS[0] = a Jaipur CA firm that handles GST notices for D2C brands. Surface: email subject lines to the firm's own list (plat:email_subject_line, fields subject line chars+words, punctuation marks, emojis: 60 chars, 9 words, 3 punctuation). Each line goes to the segment for which its deadline is real: hook 1 only to clients who have forwarded a notice (the date is the reply-by date printed on their notice, so 'your GST notice' is true); hook 2 to leads; hook 3 to new leads (the firm's offer end); hook 4 to monthly-return clients (the statutory due date); hook 5 to existing clients (the renewal price change). Every date, count, price and consequence is a [placeholder] the firm must hold; nothing resets, repeats weekly or is a countdown timer; no festival or invented event; no fear framing. New terms after an offer ends go in the preheader.
samples.text:
1. Before [date]: reply to your GST notice, or [consequence]
   Template: Before [date]: [action], or [real consequence].
2. [N] notice-review slots left for [month]
   Template: [N] [seats / units] left for [event / batch] on [date]. (date = month of the intake)
3. Rs [price] notice review ends [day, time]
   Template: [Offer] ends [day, time]. From [next day] it's [new terms]. (new terms in the preheader)
4. [Date] se pehle sales data bhejiye, warna [late fee]
   Template: [Festival] se pehle [action], warna [real consequence]. ([Festival] replaced by the statutory [Date]: the topic has no festival-linked deadline)
5. Last [N] days: renew at Rs [price]
   Template: Last [N] days to [action] at [current price].
samples.writer_note: Earlier sample tied a notice reply to Diwali (no real link), invented a 'clinic' and a 'workshop', and sent 'your GST notice' to a list that included people with none. Now each line is addressed to the segment where its deadline is real, five different sources of deadline (notice date, intake capacity, offer end, statutory due date, renewal price), no invented events. Hook 4 replaces the festival slot with the statutory date and says so; 'sales data' is the monthly-return input. All dates, counts and prices are placeholders.
